primaryRecommendations.label: Corner 1: corner-to-straight momentum

gainRange.assumption: balanced-corner: sustain session q75–q90 speed-dependent propulsion/braking and median per-lap q90–q95 lateral capability, with fixed entry/end speed and unchanged GPS line. Conditional sensitivity, not confidence bounds.
gainRange.method: Forward/backward distance-domain v² simulation at ≤2 m cells; friction ellipse checked using maximum cell speed and curvature; integrate 2Δs/(v₀+v₁). Full corner-to-straight interval; baseline speed-time alignment checked within 4% or 50 ms. No gain floor or recorded-sector cap.

primaryRecommendations.observation: The balanced-corner capability scenario saves 0.143–0.201 s across the complete corner and downstream interval. Its largest conservative contribution is minimum through corner exit; competing entry and exit profiles preserve shared boundary speeds.
primaryRecommendations.action: Keep the entry repeatable and test a more settled minimum-to-exit speed recovery. Compare the minimum-speed location and exit trace, then time the complete corner and following straight over repeated laps.

primaryRecommendations.label: Corner 2: apex recovery experiment

gainRange.assumption: If a settled exit recovers to +1 m/s over a modestly shorter distance, capped by sustained same-speed acceleration already recorded on the fastest lap; available traction remains unverified.
gainRange.method: Measured recovery window 10.6 m; a desired recovery shape compressed by up to15% is capped by the recorded acceleration and lateral-demand envelopes before computing any saving. Conditional fixed-distance integral of 1/v over the measured minimum-to-+1 m/s window. Compress the recorded speed-versus-distance shape by at most 15%, using the recorded same-speed acceleration envelope as a cap, then hold its recorded final speed to the original endpoint. Minimum speed, final speed and all speeds outside the window are preserved; no profile extrapolation. No faster lap validates this scenario, and the recovery duration is not time saved. Scenario choices are not confidence bounds or an achievable forecast; coarse GPS curvature must ease or remain stable; candidate lateral demand cannot exceed the recorded window maximum and longitudinal acceleration cannot exceed sustained same-speed measured capacity. Grip and control causes remain unverified; this is not a safe-speed instruction. Aggregation uses only disjoint endpoint-preserving scenarios.

primaryRecommendations.action: Inspect the GPS arc and RPM at the minimum. Test a settled entry and one smooth exit arc, then compare recovery onset, full corner time and the following section over repeated laps. Keep entry speed controlled while testing.

limitations: Conditional engineering sensitivity, not confidence intervals or guaranteed gains.
Recorded line retained; track width, tire forces, wind and control inputs are unmeasured.
Top speed limited to session99th percentile; absolute vehicle potential remains unknown.

Only the first corner-to-straight interval supports all tested boundary, timing, signal and feasibility constraints on these recordings. Other areas remain qualitative or retain prior small scenarios.
A single fastest lap cannot populate all speed bands robustly; larger modeled gains require the complete valid session.
Baseline integration residual is reported separately as alignment/model bias; scenario bounds do not cover all model error.
RPM-conditioned acceleration is observational and confounded; no numerical shifting benefit or engine torque curve is inferred.
